## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
Signup and reset now both enforce twelve characters, and their tests check the 11/12 boundary. But the invite validator still accepts eight-character passwords, so the "at least twelve characters" policy in the PR description is only partly enforced. Fix that before merging.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/signup.py:1 — correctness — This line raises `MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH` to 12 in signup, and `app/reset.py:1` does the same for reset. The third copy of the same validator, `app/invite.py:1`, is unchanged and still reads `MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH = 8`. It still uses `len(password) >= MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH` (`app/invite.py:5`), so an invited user who sets `"x" * 8` is accepted. `tests/test_invite.py:6-8` still asserts `length >= 8`. Could you raise `app/invite.py:1` to 12 and update `tests/test_invite.py` to the `[0, 8, 11, 12, 13]` / `>= 12` boundaries? Better still, could all three modules import one shared constant so they can't drift apart again? — Accounts created through the invite flow can still get 8–11 character passwords, which breaks the security policy this PR is meant to enforce.

## Suggestions
(none)

## Strengths
- `tests/test_reset.py:6-8` and `tests/test_signup.py:6-8` test lengths 11, 12 and 13 against the `>= 12` rule. A `>` instead of `>=` would fail at length 12, and a leftover threshold of 8 would fail at length 11.
